claims.proposition_evaluated: Between 2025-11-18 and 2026-08-27, Administration placed before City Council or a committee of Council, on a published agenda, at least two distinct proposals to change snow and ice control service, each of whose text states new spending to deliver it. The primary readings apply: the agenda-placement timing rule, Council or any committee as the body, one service package counted once, and a stated incremental cost as the cost test.
claims.interpretation_notes: PRIMARY COUNT: P=4, C=4, U=0. Rung: Supported. (1) Integrated Service Package 'Improved Accessibility - Active Pathway Snow Removal and Sidewalk Repair'. Source: FCS03158 Attachment 2, pp. 27 and 43-44, DocumentId 278877 (re-listed as 280346). Listed on the City Council agenda of 2025-11-24, item 7.2. Its text states $9,938K of 2026 incremental operating cost and 35.2 FTEs, a '$2.11 million one-time capital investment', and '$1.60 million to prioritize SNIC efforts in socially vulnerable areas'. (2) Standalone Service Package 'Parking Ban Enforcement Strategies and Resource Allocation'. Source: the same Attachment 2, pp. 25 and 34, same item. It states $100K ongoing for contracted towing during parking bans. Its text says it 'improves service levels for snow and ice control' and supports 'street blading for snow removal'. This is my borderline inclusion. (3) The 'Well Maintained City' service package. Source: CO03513 Attachment 9 (DocumentId 304812; 303388 in the 2026-08-22 capture by the order of the listing) and the report (304803/303379). Listed under item 7.1 of the Community and Public Services Committee meeting of 2026-08-31. The agenda was published by 2026-08-22 per the Internet Archive capture, and the draft was before the Agenda Review Committee on 2026-08-18. It states 'approximately $23.6 million annually in ongoing operating and $11.5 million in one-time capital'. It proposes eight-day residential blading and a Priority 1 Cycle Crew, among other changes. (4) The set of optional enhancements in CO03513 Attachment 10 (304813/303389), presented separately from the package 'to supplement' it. It contains 24 items, each with an estimated ongoing and/or one-time cost. I counted it once because it is not a service package. A reader who folds it into CO03513 gets P=3. The rung does not depend on items 2 or 4: items 1 and 3 alone give C=2. NOT COUNTED: (a) the Winter/Summer Temporary Assignment to Permanent Positions package, $1,777K (Attachment 2, pp. 45-46). It is a workforce and benefits conversion that names snow and ice only as one service it supports, not a change to snow service. (b) CS03123 / Bylaw 21283 (Community and Public Services Committee, 2026-01-19, item 7.1). I could not read it. Taproot reports it as a cut to the parking-ban fine from $250 to $150, with costed early-payment options. That is a fine change, not a snow-service change. Even if it were counted as U, it could not move the primary rung, because C is already at least 2. Motions are not counted: 2025-08-11 item 7.3, notice 2026-01-19 item 11.1, 2026-03-17 items 10.3 and 10.4, and the 2026-08-31 motions. Each package has one cost: the incremental figure its own text states. No proposal in the window establishes an excess over an identified approved budget. ALTERNATIVES: (i) Considered by a body by 2026-08-27. Items 1 and 2 count: Council dealt with item 7.2 on 2025-11-24/25 (presentations, questions, a private session and a postponement motion) and again on 2025-12-01 to 12-04. Items 3 and 4 do not: their first meeting was 2026-08-31. P=2, C=2, U=0: Supported. If the parking-ban package is excluded, C=1 and the rung is Partially supported, so this result depends on that classification. (ii) Window to 2026-10-02. Under agenda placement P=4, C=4: Supported. Under considered-by, P=4, C=4: Supported, because the committee dealt with item 7.1 on 2026-08-31 and Council dealt with item 7.9 on 2026-09-08 without debate. (iii) Pre-election start, 2025-01-01. CO03079 (2025-08-11, item 7.3; Options 2-4 costed) is the earlier version of package 1, and CS02945 (2025-06-16, unread) is the earlier version of package 2, so each counts once. P=4, C=4: Supported. (iv) City Council alone. Items 1 and 2 were on the 2025-11-24 Council agenda. CO03513 first reached a Council agenda on 2026-09-08, behind a committee report, so after the comment date. P=2, C=2: Supported; Partially supported if package 2 is excluded. (v) Separately costed options. Package 1 = 1, package 2 = 1, the Well Maintained City package = 1 (no costed sub-options), and the Attachment 10 enhancements = 24. C=27: Supported. (vi) Stricter cost reading, which requires an approved figure plus the increase against it. No proposal in the window states the approved snow and ice budget. Attachment 2 gives only 'incremental' and 'New Budget' columns. CO03513 states no baseline, and the FCS03158 report says only that unfunded packages 'would require an approved Council amendment to add to the budget'. P=4, C=0, U=0: Contradicted. With the pre-election start, CO03079 states 'The total budget for SNIC is $67 million/year' and 'Funding for these scenarios does not exist within the current budget', giving C=1: Partially supported. (vii) Exactly two. P=C=4: Partially supported. The result is Supported only if the enhancements are folded in and the parking-ban package is excluded. The finding is therefore definition-sensitive under (vi), (vii) and, depending on how package 2 is classified, (i) and (iv). A reader-facing 'already put' should name the agenda-placement rule. Separately, the 'Well Maintained City' package was 'presented here for information ahead of formal presentation during 2027-2030 budget deliberations'. Packages 1 and 2 were labelled 'Council Directed', meaning Administration prepared them because a committee or Council motion required it. Under the brief's definition both count as Administration proposals.

limitations: I could not fetch the City's eScribe filestream URLs myself (HTTP 403). All report and attachment text comes from the carried copies, so this agreement is not independent retrieval.

Attachment 2 of FCS03158 was carried in 4 of its 36 sections. The uncarried sections did not match 'snow', 'active pathway', 'parking ban' or 'SNIC'. The summary of unfunded packages (pp. 24-30) was carried whole.

Report FCS03159 and its Attachments 1-5 and 9-10 were not carried. Package 1 states a $2.11M one-time capital cost, but Attachment 8 (Unfunded Capital Profiles) shows no snow-and-ice capital profile. I could not locate where that capital request sits.

Package 1's figures do not reconcile within its own text. The summary (p. 27) and the components on p. 43 give $7.83M ongoing ($1.60M + $1.64M + $4.59M, my calculation), while the tables show $9,938K. The $2,108K difference (my calculation) matches the $2.11M one-time figure. I do not infer why.

The 2025-11-24 Council agenda marks items 7.1 and 7.2 as 'Addendum', and the minutes record them as additions at adoption. No archive or Agenda Review Committee record fixes their publication date. I used the meeting date, 2025-11-24, as the latest possible date.

I could not read the archived CO03513 files (DocumentIds 303379-303392) or the re-listed Fall 2025 files (280336, 280337, 280342), so I cannot compare their content with the live ids. Titles match as listed.

I did not read CS03123 (Community and Public Services Committee, 2026-01-19, item 7.1) or CS02945 (Community and Public Services Committee, 2025-06-16). The portal calendar is blocked to my tools, so I could not search every meeting in the period for other snow items. This does not affect the primary rung.

Background on the parked claims, for which the brief assigns no verdict: CO03513 Attachment 10 lists 'Calcium Chloride System Upgrades' at $2.5M ongoing and $4.4M one-time. None of the four committee motions of 2026-08-31 names calcium chloride.

claims.suggested_one_line: Supported, under the 'placed on a published agenda' rule: by 27 August 2026 Administration had already put at least two costed snow proposals before Council or its committee, a $9.9M sidewalk snow and repair package in November 2025 and the $23.6M-a-year 'Well Maintained City' package on the 31 August committee agenda. Neither states the existing snow budget it would add to.
claims.suggested_short_answer: Yes. Under the rule that a proposal is 'put' once it is on a published agenda, there were at least two, and four on the reviewer's count. Two costed snow packages were before Council in November 2025: $9.9M for sidewalk snow clearing and repair, and $100K for parking-ban towing. Council funded neither. The $23.6M-a-year 'Well Maintained City' package and 24 costed optional enhancements were on the agenda for the 31 August 2026 committee meeting, published by 22 August. Under the stricter test, a stated increase over an identified approved budget, the record shows none.
suggested_tldr: Placed on an agenda by 27 Aug 2026: at least 4 costed snow proposals (Supported).
Already dealt with by a body by 27 Aug 2026: 2, both in the Fall 2025 budget adjustment; Council funded neither.
No proposal in the window states the approved snow budget it would exceed. The last stated figure is $67M a year (August 2025).
The result changes under the stricter cost test or an exactly-two count.
